message: Invalid JWTs fall back to decoding with signature and expiration verification disabled, allowing forged authentication tokens.
JWTs are signed with the hardcoded, weak secret "secret", enabling offline guessing and token forgery.
The registration INSERT executes a query constructed directly from attacker-controlled username input.
The login query interpolates the supplied username directly into SQL before execution.
The transactions endpoint executes SQL containing an unvalidated attacker-controlled user_id parameter.
The transaction search query directly interpolates the attacker-controlled description search term.
Passwords are stored as fast, unsalted MD5 hashes, making recovered hashes inexpensive to crack.
The authenticated password-update endpoint selects the target from a caller-supplied user_id without requiring it to match the current user.
The forgot-password response directly returns the account reset token to the unauthenticated requester.
Password reset authorization accepts a deterministic MD5 of the public username, so any account's reset token is computable.
Attacker-controlled YAML is loaded with yaml.Loader, which can construct arbitrary Python objects and execute code.
The original upload filename is joined to the upload directory without sanitization, allowing traversal and overwrite of files outside that directory.
The public upload-serving route opens a path constructed from an unrestricted filename, allowing traversal outside the upload directory.
The transfer endpoint does not require a positive amount, so a negative transfer increases the sender's balance and debits the receiver.
QuickPay performs balance changes without validating a positive amount or checking sufficient funds, enabling balance manipulation and overdrafts.
Split-bill trusts caller-supplied payer and payee IDs and debits the selected payer without authorization or balance validation.
The receipt endpoint exposes transaction details by sequential ID without authentication or ownership checks.
An attacker-controlled transaction description is inserted unescaped into the HTML receipt response.
Authenticated user-controlled report fields are interpolated into a shell command executed with shell=True.
The service query parameter is interpolated into an os.popen shell command.
The supplied host is interpolated into a ping command executed through a shell.
The supplied domain is interpolated into an nslookup command executed with shell=True.
The webhook endpoint performs a server-side request to an unrestricted attacker-supplied URL and returns response content.
The avatar fetcher retrieves an unrestricted attacker-supplied URL, permitting access to internal services and metadata endpoints.
A caller-controlled statement filename is joined to a fixed directory and passed to send_file without containment validation.
A caller-controlled log filename is interpolated into an open path, allowing files outside /var/log to be read.
Untrusted XML is parsed with external entity resolution and network access enabled, allowing local-file disclosure and SSRF.
Base64-decoded attacker input is passed to pickle.loads, enabling arbitrary code execution.
Arbitrary request keys are assigned to any selected User object, permitting changes to role, password hash, balance, and other sensitive fields.
An attacker-controlled template is evaluated by render_template_string, enabling server-side code execution.
The unauthenticated redirect endpoint redirects directly to an arbitrary caller-supplied URL.
Any authenticated user can list all accounts including password hashes, balances, roles, and profile data because no administrator authorization is enforced.
Any authenticated user can delete an arbitrary account because the admin route performs no role check.
An attacker-controlled regular expression is evaluated against every username without complexity or timeout controls.
Attacker-controlled expression input is passed directly to eval.
Attacker-controlled script input is executed directly with exec.
Attacker-controlled format input is compiled as Python code and executed.
Administrative access relies on a plaintext master password embedded in source code.
A security-critical administrator check uses assert and disappears when Python optimization is enabled.
The dashboard response returns embedded API and AWS access keys to any authenticated user.
Multiple API, cloud, database, JWT, GitHub, and webhook credentials are embedded directly in source code.
The server reflects every Origin while allowing credentials, permitting attacker-controlled origins to make credentialed cross-origin requests.
Internal exception details are returned directly in HTTP 500 responses.
The externally bound Flask server runs with debug mode enabled, exposing sensitive diagnostics and potentially the interactive debugger.
The authentication cookie is explicitly readable by JavaScript and allowed over plaintext connections.
